message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so H⁻ is unstable in vacuum) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | Phase | Gas |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L/mol |
| | Density | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.0000899 g/cm³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 28.836 J/(mol·K) |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.025 kJ/mol |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1,200 m/s (at 20 °C) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; H₂ is a diatomic molecule with a single σ bond |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (H⁻) depending on context |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ/mol) |
| | Redox potential | Standard reduction potential of H⁺/H₂ is 0 V (by definition) |
| | Solubility in water | ~0.0006 g/100 g at 25 °C (very low) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; often used as a solvent itself (liquid H₂) |
| **Spectroscopic & Quantum** | Rotational constant (H₂) | 59.3 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Ionization potential (H atom) | 13.598 eV |
| | Ground state | 1s¹ (doublet) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 1 % of natural hydrogen |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion and radiolabeling |
| **Applications & Roles** | Fuel cell fuel | H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (electrochemical) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ |
| | Metallurgy | Used to reduce metal oxides, produce high‑purity metals |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydrogenation of alkenes, reduction of nitriles, etc. |
| | Astrophysics | Primary element in stars; fusion produces He |
| | Environmental | Potential clean energy carrier; low CO₂ emissions when produced from renewables |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range | 4–75 % H₂ in air |
| | Explosion limit | 4 % (lower) – 75 % (upper) |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can displace oxygen in confined spaces (asphyxiation risk) |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders, cryogenic tanks, or metal hydrides |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms bonds with almost all elements, especially oxygen and metals.
- **Energy‑dense**: In terms of mass, hydrogen has the highest energy content per unit mass (≈120 MJ/kg).
- **Versatile**: From fuels to fertilizers, hydrogen plays a central role in both industrial chemistry and emerging clean‑energy technologies.
- **Safety**: Its wide flammability range and low density make it a potential hazard in poorly ventilated areas.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
